summary:
AstroGuardian-AI is an intelligent, offline-first astronaut health monitoring and early warning system designed for long-duration space missions.
 * What we developed: A robust two-layer architecture combining a deterministic Python/FastAPI analysis engine (Layer 1) for personal z-score baseline tracking and live NOAA solar radiation threat assessment, paired with a GPT-OSS-20B language assistant (Layer 2) for plain-language explanations. It features tailored role-based interfaces for astronauts, crew medical officers, and ground flight surgeons.
 * How it addresses the challenge: It tackles the isolation of deep space exploration by functioning entirely offline without continuous internet dependency. It detects subtle health drifts unique to each individual rather than relying on generic averages, and includes fail-safe caching to handle sensor and network outages safely.
 * Why it is important: As humanity pushes toward lunar bases and Mars, communication delays with Earth make real-time medical guidance impossible. AstroGuardian-AI provides autonomous, reliable, and explainable health oversight to protect astronaut safety, mitigate radiation hazards, and safeguard mission success.
details: 🚀 Project Name "AstroGuardian-AI" 1. What does it do and how does it work? AstroGuardian-AI is an intelligent, offline-first astronaut health monitoring and early warning system designed for long-duration space missions. How it works: The system operates on a robust Two-Layer Architecture: * Layer 1 (Deterministic Analysis Engine): Built using Python, FastAPI, Pandas, and NumPy, this core layer continuously analyzes astronaut biometrics against personal z-score baselines (tracking how an individual drifts from their own normal, rather than generic human averages) and fixed, scientifically cited safety limits. It also factors in live NOAA solar radiation storm data and multi-day patterns (like sleep debt and fatigue). It alone determines the health status tier (GREEN, YELLOW, RED, or UNKNOWN). * Layer 2 (Language Assistant / LLM): Powered by GPT-OSS-20B, this layer translates technical findings into plain-language answers for the crew and flight surgeons. Crucially, the LLM can never alter or override alert tiers, ensuring safety-critical decisions remain 100% deterministic and reliable. The system also features role-specific screens: the Astronaut view (Today), the Crew Medical Officer view (Crew Triage), and the Ground Flight Surgeon view (Comms Window). 2. What benefits does it have? * Zero Dependence on Continuous Internet: Fully functional offline-first architecture designed to run locally on spacecraft computers and sync telemetry during ground communication windows. * Personalized Baselines: Eliminates false alarms by detecting subtle health drifts unique to each astronaut. * Real-World Data Integration: Incorporates live NOAA solar radiation feeds and real NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) multi-omics blood test data from the SpaceX Inspiration4 mission (OSD-575 and OSD-569), combined with simulator models calibrated to published ISS studies. * Fail-Safe Reliability: Cached offline fallback states ensure sensor outages or network drops never compromise crew safety. 3. What is the intended impact of the project? As humanity pushes further into deep space (such as Artemis lunar bases and eventual crewed Mars missions), communication delays with Earth make real-time medical guidance impossible. AstroGuardian-AI empowers crews with autonomous, reliable, and explainable health oversight, ensuring early risk detection, protecting against radiation hazards, and safeguarding astronaut performance and well-being in isolated environments. 4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use? * Frontend: React, Tailwind CSS, Recharts (built with Vite) * Backend & API: Python, FastAPI * AI & Data Engine: Pandas, NumPy, GPT-OSS-20B via OpenAI-compatible API (Groq for cloud demo, local deployment ready for spacecraft) * Databases: SQLite (local/onboard) and Neon PostgreSQL (cloud demo) * External APIs & Data: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC), NASA DONKI API, and NASA OSDR CSV datasets * Quality Assurance & DevOps: Pytest, Vitest, GitHub Actions CI, Vercel 5. How is your project creative? AstroGuardian-AI uniquely bridges the gap between raw space telemetry and clinical actionability by introducing a strict safety separation between heavy data analytics and generative AI. While most AI health tools rely purely on LLMs (which are prone to hallucinations), our system uses a deterministic math engine (Layer 1) to make absolute medical and safety decisions, using the LLM strictly as an interactive explanatory companion (Layer 2). Additionally, it weaves live real-time space weather (NOAA proton flux) directly into everyday crew health risk assessments. 6. What factors did your team consider? * Connectivity & Bandwidth Constraints: Designed from the ground up to operate offline with minimal computational footprints and intelligent data caching. * Data Integrity & Robustness: Implemented automated checks to handle messy real-world datasets (e.g., cleaning corrupted CSV columns and correcting mislabeled lab units in NASA OSDR files). * Role-Based Privacy & Security: Ensured sensitive medical data is properly segregated, allowing astronauts personal self-checks while giving Crew Medical Officers and Ground Flight Surgeons the necessary overview to triage fleet or crew health safely.
